analysis:
The PR changes only a test file, ProviderModelSwitchTests.swift, with new head lines about 189-229. It adds the test theDaemonStateReportsTheFilterACommittedSwitchApplied(accepted:). That test checks the daemon state file reports the enabled_models filter after a committed model switch, and that none is reported after a refused commit. No production code changed. The supplied units are the base text only, and the patch excerpt is truncated (patch_excerpt_complete=false). I could not see the end of the new test, nor the production change that populates the daemon state with the applied filter. The test itself shows no new attack surface. It uses the MockCoordinator and temporary directories, with no secrets, network exposure or authorization logic.

For the threat model, the switch/drain/commit flow touches TB-002 (coordinator-to-provider websocket) and TB-011 (authorization). Possible concerns are model advertisement integrity and stale authorization, which relate to T-053, T-027 and T-012. The base tests already cover weight-hash binding, rollback on rejection, and a routing-receipt barrier. The new test only adds an observability assertion on the state file. The state file is written under the provider's own directory, and the supplied evidence shows no sensitive data in it. No visible T-041 cache issue is touched.

Remaining question for integration: whether the paired production change that publishes the applied filter in the daemon state is safe. That would be state.json content and file permissions, and the filter being restored on refusal. It is outside the supplied units, so I flag this as a coverage limit rather than a finding.
